_: WHAT ALREADY SERVES THIS. A register keyed by the QUESTION a builder asks, not by the file that answers it.
_why: There is a standing rule in this yard: BEFORE BUILDING ON A SURFACE, ASK WHAT
ALREADY SERVES IT. It has been a rule with no instrument behind it, and on 29 Aug
2026 the same fault happened twice in one session.
WORKS.semantics.json was written to hold what each figure wrote — six figures, twelve
works, every url null — while LIBRARY.json sat in the repo holding 550 works across 52
rooms, most of them with translator, edition and Gutenberg number. Its path was in the
unindexed list, read twice, and passed over both times, because the index says WHERE a
file is and not WHAT NEED IT MEETS.
And MANUAL.md was written for a reader when the request had been for an operator's map.
EVERY REGISTER IN THIS FLEET IS KEYED BY PATH. To learn whether a corpus exists you
must read 181 glosses and recognise one. Nobody does that, so things get built twice.
_law: A CAPABILITY THAT IS NOT IN THIS FILE WILL BE BUILT AGAIN. That is not a threat, it is what happened.
_howToUse: BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING, look up the need here.
· If it is here and `servedBy` is populated — READ THOSE FILES FIRST. The thing
probably exists and needs joining up, not building.
· If it is here and `servedBy` is null — nothing serves it. Build, and fill this in.
· IF THE NEED IS NOT HERE AT ALL, THAT IS THE FINDING. Add the entry before you write
a line of code. Naming the need is most of the work of not duplicating it.
`doesNotAnswer` is as load-bearing as `servedBy`. A register that says what it covers
and not what it omits invites the second mistake: trusting it too far. LIBRARY.json
holds every citation and cannot tell you whether a quotation is really in the work.
_verification: probe-serves.mjs checks that every file named here exists in SOURCES.json, and reports any need whose server has gone missing. AN ENTRY POINTING AT A FILE THAT IS NOT THERE IS WORSE THAN NO ENTRY.

the corpus.question: What did a figure actually write, and where can it be read?
the corpus.answers: 52 rooms, 550 works, 31 MB of text. Each work carries a title, a section and a SOURCE — for most, translator, edition and Project Gutenberg number.
the corpus.doesNotAnswer: Whether a given quotation is really IN the work it is attributed to. Nothing here can, short of holding the text and searching it.
the corpus.note: THIS IS THE ONE THAT WAS BUILT TWICE. If you are about to write a register of what figures wrote, you are writing this one again.

whether a citation can be traced.question: Can this quotation be checked back to a findable edition?
whether a citation can be traced.answers: Every work graded CITED, DATED, THIN, EMPTY or LINKED, with a sentence per room saying what it still needs.
whether a citation can be traced.doesNotAnswer: Whether the cited edition is the right one for a particular line. A translator's choices are not in scope.

moving a citation onto works that lack o.question: A room's works have no source and I know the edition. Now what?
moving a citation onto works that lack o.answers: Stamps a source onto every stored work in a manifest that has none. Report-only unless --write, never overwrites, never touches a link-out.
moving a citation onto works that lack o.doesNotAnswer: What the edition IS. It will not guess, and run without --source it reports the gap and exits non-zero.

the surfaces.question: Where can a person act on this system, and what reaches each place?
the surfaces.answers: Every named interaction point, its engine, what it costs, and four booleans: counted, memory, dial, voice.
the surfaces.doesNotAnswer: Page2's own points, the gameroom's, or the reading vaults' — all entered as pages rather than surfaces and named as gaps in the register itself.

the voice.question: How does a figure speak, what does it cost, and what must not be touched?
the voice.answers: The cache-key formula, the two registers and why the counsel never caches, the roster columns a voice is assembled from, the failure modes and what each SOUNDS like, the dial's measured gap, the ear's dials, what a spoken turn costs.
the voice.doesNotAnswer: Whether the deployed bundle matches. SPEECH.md was read from the code on 28 Aug; where they disagree the code is right.

what a figure says and refuses.question: What governs how a figure behaves in conversation?
what a figure says and refuses.answers: The governing logic every mount inherits, the registers, the moves, and §4.6 on what a figure may remember.
what a figure says and refuses.doesNotAnswer: The counsel chamber's prompt. cnsGo runs its own counselSys() in Page1.html and the chat core knows nothing about it — two prompts exist.

every document in the fleet.question: Where is a document, is it reachable, and what is it?
every document in the fleet.answers: 181 paths with a gloss and a verified HTTP status, plus a drift report naming what is unreachable and what nobody has described.
every document in the fleet.doesNotAnswer: WHAT NEED A FILE MEETS. It is keyed by path. That gap is the reason this file exists.

the roster.question: Who are the figures, and what is known about each?
the roster.answers: 1,011 souls with 21 columns — Gender, Dialect and Voice drive speech; Appearance and Dress drive the plate.
the roster.doesNotAnswer: What they wrote. The `Links` column is a Wikipedia SEARCH-BOX url generated from the name and cites nothing.
the roster.note: Column zero is Rank. READ THE NAME BY HEADER. BC dates are stored as NEGATIVE NUMBERS, not as letters — Caesar's Death-Date is "-44".

the plates.question: Which figures have art, and where did it come from?
the plates.answers: Keys, variants, scenes, gaps, accepted mismatches — and the generation seeds and crop notes.
the plates.doesNotAnswer: Whether a plate HOLDS. That judgement needs a person; the pipeline says so.

what the fleet has published.question: Did the scheduled thing actually fire?
what the fleet has published.answers: Intent beside reality, per tube: cadence, status, fire count, last-fired date.
what the fleet has published.doesNotAnswer: Whether what fired was any good.

the book.question: What chapters exist and what state are they in?
the book.answers: Every chapter measured against the register: state, size, bands, the day it landed.

the vocabulary.question: What does this word mean on this ship?
the vocabulary.answers: The fleet's terms — soul, key, plate, spell, register, probe, the Silent Signature, empty glass, the water between. MANUEL covers Page2's own parts.
the vocabulary.doesNotAnswer: Page1's parts, which is what PAGE1.md is for.

how to use the site.question: What is Amenti and how does a reader use a room?
how to use the site.answers: All eleven doors, the five modes and what to bring to each, and the things a reader cannot discover by clicking.
how to use the site.note: AIMED OUTWARD. The crew's version of the same page is PAGE1.md, and confusing the two is the second thing that was built wrong on 29 Aug.

how to edit Page1.question: I am about to change the flagship. What will bite me?
how to edit Page1.answers: The bundle, the wildcard reset, duplicate selectors, the six real data-page sections against eleven nav tabs, and the four conversation surfaces that do not share a prompt.
how to edit Page1.doesNotAnswer: The enumeration of controls — that is SURFACES.json, deliberately.

the yard's open work.question: What is still undone, and what has been recorded but not chased?
the yard's open work.answers: Sixty-nine moves, each ending in a check the captain can perform by opening something.
the yard's open work.note: The slip is kept BY HAND and read at the TOP of a session. It lives at the ROOT of Amenti.live — this entry pointed at the briefs repo until 5 Sep, where no such file exists. slip/ holds items that GRADUATED out of the slip because they grew phases. SESSION-2026-08-01.md is a shop-floor account of that day and claims nothing about today.

what the repo actually contains.question: What is really in there — not what a document claims?
what the repo actually contains.answers: Files, globals, who loads whom, who calls whom, endpoints, load order. Its findings.adrift names files a page loads that nobody calls.
what the repo actually contains.doesNotAnswer: Anything about intent. The scanner observes and has no opinion.

a post that names a real person.question: Is this safe to publish with a dead person's name on it?
a post that names a real person.answers: Refuses an unsourced quotation, a note written in the figure's voice, a figure not on the roster, and anyone inside the living-memory line.
a post that names a real person.doesNotAnswer: Whether a sourced quotation is REAL. It cannot check the corpus; it forces the citation to exist so a fabrication is deliberate rather than accidental.
a post that names a real person.note: COULD BE WIRED TO LIBRARY.json and check the source against the corpus. It is not, yet.

the panes.question: What operator surfaces exist in Fleet-Documents?
the panes.answers: 19 panes, registered once. The Harbor builds its grid from the registry rather than a hand-typed list.
the panes.note: READ THE REGISTRY, NEVER RETYPE IT. The grid was hand-written until 28 Aug and held 13 cards against 18 panes.

the workers.question: What runs server-side, on what schedule, with what bindings?
the workers.answers: Six Workers: crons, bindings, secret NAMES. No values.
the workers.doesNotAnswer: Their source, which is in a private repo.

rate limiting and spend ceilings.question: Can the gate refuse a flood through one door without starving another?
rate limiting and spend ceilings.note: NOTHING SERVES THIS. RULING-ONE-ENGINE-SEPARATE-LANES rules the shape and no code exists. The proxy today answers anyone who can load a page, with no origin check, no rate limit and no spend ceiling. NO AD RUNS BEFORE THE GATE CAN SAY NO.

prompt caching.question: Is the 2,244-token system prompt being re-sent every turn?
prompt caching.note: NOTHING SERVES THIS. BRIEF-THE-PROMPT-NOBODY-CACHES measures a 33% saving and the builders return { head, tail }. `window.claude.acceptsSystemTail` is not set, so it does not engage.

counting what a visit costs.question: How much did a reader's visit actually spend?
counting what a visit costs.answers: The modelled cost of an hour, both halves, measured rather than estimated.
counting what a visit costs.note: PARTIALLY SERVED. amenti-visits.js is NOT WIRED INTO Page1 — AmentiVisits.begin and .end appear nowhere in the file — and of five conversation surfaces only one is counted.

_stillToName: This register is as good as the needs somebody has thought to write down, and it was
opened with twenty. THE ONES THAT MATTER ARE THE ONES NOT HERE, and there is no probe
that can find them: a walk can verify that a named file exists and cannot invent the
So the discipline is the whole instrument. When a session begins a build, the first
move is to look the need up here. When it is not here, the entry goes in FIRST.
